### What's new
- **No more crash from the macOS window tab bar.** If macOS was set to prefer tabs when opening documents, or you chose **View › Show Tab Bar**, Silica's windows showed the system tab bar: its + button crashed Silica, and the bar covered the top of the sidebar, hiding the Find in Project field. Silica's windows no longer use macOS window tabs, so the bar and its menu items are gone; your files keep their own tabs as before. - **⌃Tab and ⌃⇧Tab are no longer reserved.** **Settings › Keybinds** kept them for switching window tabs, which Silica no longer has, so you can now give them to any command.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Split view.** **View › Split Right** (⌘D) and **View › Split Down** (⇧⌘D) divide the editor into panes, as many as you want, each with its own tabs. Drag the line between two panes to resize them, drag a tab onto another pane to move it there, and ⌥-click a file in the Explorer, or choose **Open in New Pane** from its menu, to open it in a pane of its own. A file can be open in several panes, each with its own cursor and scroll position, so you can write Markdown in one pane and watch its preview in the other. **View › Focus Next Pane** (⌥⌘→) and **View › Focus Previous Pane** (⌥⌘←) move between panes, and **View › Close Pane** (⌃⌘W) closes one and moves its tabs to the pane beside it. The status bar has buttons for both splits, the layout comes back when you reopen the project, and the keybinds can be changed in **Settings › Keybinds**. - **A warning when a file with unsaved edits changes on disk.** When another app changes a file you are editing (a branch switch, a formatter), a bar over the editor says so and the tab's dot turns orange. **Revert** shows the file as it is on disk, and **Keep My Edits** keeps your version, so saving writes it over the one on disk. Before, you only found out when you saved. - **The view stays still when you type in a long file.** After jumping far into a file, typing could shift the text by a line or more, and Return could leave the top lines of the view blank.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Git support.** In a git repository, the file tree marks changed files and the status bar names the branch. **View › Source Control** (⌃⇧G) lists staged and unstaged changes: select one to see its diff in the file's tab, inline or side by side, and stage, unstage or discard whole files or single changes. From the panel you can commit, amend or undo the last commit, fetch, pull and push, switch, create, merge, rename and delete branches, and work with stashes. **View › Show File History** lists a file's commits, and **View › Line Blame** shows who last changed the current line. A merge or rebase that stops for conflicts gets a banner to continue or abort, and a bar in the editor accepts either side. It uses the git you have installed and stays hidden without it. - **Configurable keybinds.** **Settings › Keybinds** has Silica, VS Code and Xcode presets, and you can record your own keybind for any command there. Keybinds work on any keyboard layout, Settings warns when one would clash with another command, and menus, tooltips and hints show your current keys. Contributed by Mitch Treece. - **A `silica` command for the terminal.** `silica .` opens the current folder as a project, and `silica <file>` opens a file in its project. Install it from **Settings › General › Command Line**; installing Silica with Homebrew sets it up for you. - **Quick Open opens the file you picked.** Pressing Return opened the top result instead of the row selected with the arrow keys. Contributed by Hernan Fernandez.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Copy Relative Path on editor tabs.** Right-click a tab and choose **Copy Relative Path** to copy the file's path from the workspace folder, as the file tree already offers. It shows for files inside the workspace. - **Find highlights the matches on every search.** After the first search in a tab, later searches showed the match count and dimmed the text but highlighted nothing. Every search now highlights its matches. - **The find bar no longer covers the first lines.** Opening it at the top of a file used to hide line 1, even when the first match was there. The text now moves down with the bar, and back up when it closes. - **Project dotfiles aren't dimmed.** In a git repository, the file tree used to dim every dotfile, so folders like `.github` looked hidden. Now it dims only what is gitignored. In a folder that isn't a repository, dotfiles are still dimmed. - **A narrow window no longer cuts off the sidebar and editor.** Shrinking a workspace window could clip the left of the file tree and the right of the editor. The sidebar now gives up width so both fit, and grows back when the window does.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Runs on macOS 15.** Silica now needs macOS 15 or later, down from macOS 26. Liquid Glass came with macOS 26, so on earlier versions the cards, tabs and buttons are plain, with a border and a shadow. - **Syntax highlighting for Dart.** `.dart` files are highlighted, and so are `dart` code blocks in the Markdown preview. That makes 27 languages. - **Choose a translucent or opaque window.** **Background** in **Settings › General** is **Translucent**, a frosted blur of what's behind the window, or **Opaque**, the solid window color. - **Turn the glass effect off.** With **Glass effect** off in **Settings › General**, the cards, tabs and buttons sit on plain bordered cards instead of Liquid Glass. - **The Markdown preview fills its pane.** The text used to stop at a narrow column in the middle. It now runs the full width of the pane. - **A double-click in a preview selects a word.** In a Markdown or CSV preview it used to switch to the source and put the cursor on that line, which made it impossible to select a word there. - **Settings looks like other Mac settings windows.** It is rebuilt on the system's own sidebar and grouped lists, and on macOS 27 its pickers show as capsule tabs.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **A terminal under the editor.** **View › Terminal** (**⌃`**) opens your shell in the project's folder, in a glass card below the editor. Drag the gap between the two to resize it. The arrow in the card's header hides the terminal while the shell carries on, and the trash, **Kill Terminal**, ends it. **View › Clear Terminal** (**⌘K**) clears it. - **Several terminals, each in a tab.** The **+** button in the terminal's header, or **View › New Terminal** (**⌃⇧`**), starts another shell, and from the second on each gets a tab in the header. Click a tab to bring its terminal forward, drag it to reorder, and middle-click it or right-click and choose **Kill Terminal** to end it. While a terminal has the keyboard, **⌃Tab**, **⌃⇧Tab**, **⇧⌘]** and **⇧⌘[** step through the terminals; from the editor they still step through the file tabs. - **Follow links in the terminal with a ⌘ click.** Hold ⌘ over a web address or a file path to underline it and see where it goes in the card's header. A path to a file that exists opens in a Silica tab, at the line printed after it. - **Show and hide the terminal from the title bar.** A terminal button sits at the end of the title bar, whatever is open and whether or not the sidebar is showing. It is tinted while the terminal is showing. - **Recent projects show their Finder icons.** The **Recent Projects** list in the welcome window now shows each folder as Finder does, with custom folder icons and packages looking like what they are. - **A dragged tab stays in view.** Dropping a tab after a drag that scrolled the tab bar could leave the tab out of sight. The bar now scrolls to where the tab landed.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Preview HTML files.** **View › Show Preview** (**⇧⌘V**) and the title bar toggle now work for .html, .htm and .xhtml files as they do for Markdown. The page is shown as a browser would show it, with its styles, images and scripts, and with your unsaved changes. Web links open in your browser and links to project files open in a Silica tab. - **Preview CSV and TSV files as a table.** The same toggle shows a .csv or .tsv file as a table with a header row that stays at the top and numeric columns aligned right. Double-click a row to go to its line in the source. Very large files are cut off at 100,000 cells, with a note saying how many rows there are. - **PDFs open in the editor.** A PDF file now opens in its own tab instead of showing as a binary file. A password-protected PDF asks for its password. - **Video files play in the editor.** Videos open in a player, with the picture's size, length and file size beneath it. Each tab keeps its place in its video, and a video pauses when you switch away from its tab. - **Animated GIFs play in the image viewer.** A GIF, animated PNG or animated WebP now plays in its tab, where only its first frame was shown. - **Diff and patch files are highlighted.** .diff, .patch and .rej files, and diff code blocks in the Markdown preview, show added lines in green and removed lines in red in every theme. - **Drag files and folders out of the sidebar.** Drag a row from the file tree to another app as you would from Finder: Terminal inserts its path, and Finder or the Desktop gets a copy. The file is never moved. - **Drag the project folder from its name.** Hovering the project name at the top of the sidebar shows the folder's Finder icon. Drag it to Terminal to insert the project's path, or to Finder to copy the folder. - **Reveal a tab's file in the explorer.** Right-click a tab and choose **Reveal in Explorer** to open the folders above the file and select it in the file tree. - **Close a tab with a middle click.** - **Set the sidebar's font size.** **Settings › Fonts & Colors** has a new **Sidebar** group with a size from 9 to 20 pt, separate from the editor font. The file tree and the Find in Project results follow it. - **Folders show their Finder icons in the file tree.** Custom folder icons appear, and packages such as .xcodeproj look like what they are. - **Sidebar buttons highlight under the pointer.** The Collapse Folders, Search and sidebar toggle buttons now show a soft fill on hover, like toolbar buttons in system apps. - **Large Markdown previews no longer hold up the window.** The preview is now prepared in the background.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Parent folders stay in view in the file tree.** Scrolled deep into a project, the open folders that contain the rows you're looking at now stay pinned at the top of the tree. Click a pinned folder to scroll back to it. It's on by default; turn it off in **Settings › General**. - **Switch tabs from the keyboard.** **⌃Tab** and **⌃⇧Tab** (or **⇧⌘]** and **⇧⌘[**) step through the open tabs, going round from either end to the other. The commands are also in the **View** menu as Select Next Tab and Select Previous Tab. - **Scroll the tab bar with a mouse wheel.** With the pointer over the tab bar, an ordinary mouse wheel now scrolls the tabs sideways, so tabs past the end of the bar can be reached without a trackpad. - **The tab bar keeps the active tab in view.** Resizing the window or the sidebar no longer scrolls the tab row back to its first tab. - **Tabs fade out at the ends of the tab bar.** A tab scrolled part of the way out now fades instead of being cut off flat. - **The minimap is hidden by default.** Turn it back on with **View › Minimap** or in **Settings › Editor**.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Drag tabs to reorder them.** Drag an editor tab along the tab bar and the tabs it passes slide aside. With more tabs than fit, holding it near either end scrolls the bar. - **A steadier selection in the file tree.** The selected file or folder is now always highlighted in grey. It used to turn blue at times, such as after renaming a file.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Runs on macOS 26.** Silica now needs macOS 26 or later, down from macOS 27. - **A nicer installer.** The DMG opens to a window with Silica and your Applications folder side by side, so installing is one drag.
If you already have 0.1.0, Silica will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

The first release of Silica, a lightweight code editor for macOS, made of glass.
### What's in it
- **Projects.** Open a folder to get a window with a file tree that follows changes on disk and dims what your `.gitignore` excludes. Create, rename and trash files right in the tree, and filter it as you type. - **Quick Open (⌘P)** with fuzzy matching, and **Find in Project (⇧⌘F)**. - **Syntax highlighting** for 25 languages, including Swift, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C, C++ and Markdown. - **Nine color themes**, each with a light and a dark palette: Atom One, GitHub, Xcode, Solarized, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, Rosé Pine and Dracula. - **Markdown preview (⇧⌘V)**, with highlighted code blocks. - **Editing tools**: tabs, line numbers, indent guides, a minimap, word wrap, Go to Line (⌘L), toggle comment (⌘/), and moving or duplicating lines (⌥↑ ⌥↓). - Projects **reopen their tabs** where you left them, and recent projects are on the welcome window. - **Open With** in Finder, the Dock icon and `open -a Silica` all open files and folders in Silica.
### Installing
Open the DMG and drag Silica to Applications. Silica needs macOS 27 or later.
From now on, Silica checks for updates once a day and installs them for you. You can also use **Silica › Check for Updates…**, or turn automatic checks off in Settings › General.
### Feedback
This is an early release, so expect some rough edges. If you find a bug or have an idea, please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).
